record.context_brief: Global synchrony with signed random edges
record.original_question: Let A be an n x n random symmetric matrix with zero diagonal and off-diagonal entries independently equal to +1 with probability 1/2 + delta and -1 with probability 1/2 - delta, where delta >= (1 + epsilon)*sqrt((log n)/(2n)) for fixed epsilon > 0. Is A globally synchronizing with high probability as n -> infinity (in the sense that all local minima of E(theta) = (1/2) sum_{i,j=1}^n Aij(1 - cos(theta_i - theta_j)) are global minima at constant phases)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4 (Global Synchrony with negative edges). Given any ε > 0, the n × n random matrix A with zero diagonal and off-diagonal entries given by Aij = 1 with probability 1/2 + δ, and -1 with probability 1/2 - δ, with δ ≥ (1 + ε) sqrt(log n/(2n)), is globally synchronizing with high probability.
In this context, we are happy to report on two lines of progress: Conjecture 4 was answered by McRae in [McR25], following up on work of Rakoto Endor and Waldspurger [EW24].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and fix $\varepsilon>0$. Let $A=(A_{ij})$ be a random $n\times n$ symmetric matrix with zero diagonal, whose off-diagonal entries $\{A_{ij}:1\le i<j\le n\}$ are independent and satisfy
$$\Pr(A_{ij}=+1)=\tfrac12+\delta,\qquad \Pr(A_{ij}=-1)=\tfrac12-\delta,$$
where $\delta=\delta(n)\ge (1+\varepsilon)\sqrt{\dfrac{\log n}{2n}}$.

Define the homogeneous Kuramoto-type energy on the $n$-torus $\mathbb{T}^n$ by
$$E(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n)=\tfrac12\sum_{i,j=1}^n A_{ij}\bigl(1-\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j)\bigr).$$
Call $A$ "globally synchronizing" if every local minimum of $E$ is a global minimum at which all phases are constant (i.e. $\theta_1=\theta_2=\cdots=\theta_n$ modulo $2\pi$).

Question: Prove or disprove that, with probability tending to $1$ as $n\to\infty$, the random matrix $A$ is globally synchronizing.
artifact.category_tag: global synchronization of signed random networks
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been resolved affirmatively. Building on work of Rakoto Endor and Waldspurger, McRae (2025) established benign landscape results for synchronization with signed/negative edges via normalized Laplacian techniques, confirming the global synchrony statement with high probability under the stated threshold on $\delta$.

status_evidence.title: Benign landscapes for synchronization on spheres via normalized Laplacian matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Proves benign landscape (every second-order critical point is a global optimum / synchronization) for signed random network models including Erdős–Rényi-type signed adjacency matrices with negative edges, in optimal asymptotic regimes.
status_evidence.claim: McRae's 2025 work resolves the global synchrony conjecture for the signed random matrix model at the stated threshold.

status_evidence.title: Global Synchronization (problems 3-5) | Randomstrasse 101
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the conjecture on global synchrony with negative edges and notes follow-up progress by Rakoto Endor–Waldspurger and McRae.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is recorded as resolved by McRae following Endor–Waldspurger.
